Subject: DPA / transfers — initial ask and timelines

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — NimbusHealth is keen to move forward but legal has flagged international transfer language in your DPA. Specifically:

- We need confirmation you can execute the UK IDTA addendum (or equivalent bridging language) and also support EU SCCs where required.
- Please provide a short transfer impact appendix describing which mechanisms will be used for EU -> US processing, fallback plan if SCCs are not accepted in a jurisdiction, and whether you can support localisation requirements per country.
- We require an up-to-date subprocessors list and timing for notification of new subprocessors (we typically ask for 30 days).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and a one-page note on how you handle third-party subprocessor SCCs.

Can you share a consolidated approach and an estimate for when legal can expect final DPA redlines for signature? Procurement would like to close this in the next two weeks.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: RE: DPA / transfers — redlines + transfer appendix (draft)

Sofia / team — attached is my first pass. Key points called out in the PDF redline:

- We recommend SCCs (EU Commission 2021) as the baseline for EU transfers with a UK IDTA addendum clause that mirrors the core obligations and adds the UK-specific supplementary terms.
- Suggested bridging language for UK IDTA: a short addendum template that can be appended on signature or executed together.
- If a customer requires on-prem/localisation, we flag those as "localisation exceptions" and propose an SOW / addendum rather than DPA-level change.
- Subprocessor notification: we accept 30 days by default; we can entertain 15 days for strategic customers but need explicit contract language and an approved escalation path for emergency onboarding.
- Fallback: where SCCs are not permitted, we propose a documented mitigation plan (technical controls: encryption at rest + in transit, strict access controls, limited data retention) and a commit to work with the customer on a targeted mitigation plan.

I've attached: transfer_risk_appendix_karthik_redlines.pdf (annotated), and a short sample UK addendum paragraph inside the appendix. I flagged three clauses for Procurement to watch (Data Transfer Mechanisms; Subprocessor Notification; Audit & Evidence).

(attachment: transfer_risk_appendix_karthik_redlines.pdf)

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel (Contracts), Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

On a process note: we prefer delivering the final DPA via DocuSign. If Nimbus wants AdobeSign, we'll accommodate but DocuSign gives us better envelope tracking for multiple signatories.

Thanks Karthik / Sofia — I reviewed the draft appendix and the bridging language. A few items from NimbusLegal / Procurement:

- Subprocessor notification: 30 days is acceptable, but we require a right to object with a 15-day cure period and the option to suspend processing for the impacted data flows if unresolved. Please confirm.
- SCCs + UK addendum: acceptable in principle. We will need a completed SCC execution log for any subprocessor that receives patient data; can you provide a csv/list of subprocessors with signed SCC record or evidence?
- SOC 2: please share a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (or a summary + date).

If you can incorporate the objection/cure language in the subprocessor clause and provide the evidence items, Procurement is OK to proceed to signature. We prefer DocuSign.

Best,
Elena
